All in the Family. A sitcom that aired on CBS from nineteen seventy-one to nineteen seventy-nine, starring Carroll O'Connor as Archie Bunker, a bigoted, working-class Queens ironworker whose clashes with his liberal son-in-law and family became the vehicle for satirizing American racism, sexism, and class conflict. The show proved that sitcoms could tackle taboo social issues head-on and that mainstream television audiences would embrace comedy rooted in cultural controversy.

Archie Bunker was a lovable bigot whose prejudices drove the show's conflicts and satirical humor. Carroll O'Connor created a memorable adversary in Mike Stivic, Archie's liberal son-in-law played by Rob Reiner, whose presence represented progressive values and the generation gap. The show tackled racism, antisemitism, women's liberation, gay rights, and other cultural flashpoints head-on, using Archie's ignorance as the comedy. It aired during the height of the Vietnam War and the civil rights movement, providing a comedic mirror to real social turbulence.

All in the Family spawned multiple spinoffs, most notably The Jeffersons, following Archie's Black neighbors moving to a wealthier neighborhood. The show won four consecutive Emmy Awards for Outstanding Comedy Series from nineteen seventy-one to nineteen seventy-four. However, it remained controversial; many viewers missed the satire and embraced Archie's views, complicating the show's cultural role.
